In Thailand and Myanmar many young men live for a few weeks or months as monks in a monastery.

teile.einleitung: Uluru is a huge red rock in the middle of Australia. It is one of the best-known landmarks of the country. For the Anangu, the Aboriginal people of this area, it is a holy place.
wichtigste: Uluru stands in the Northern Territory, almost in the middle of Australia.
It is a mighty rock of sandstone and glows reddish.
It rises about 350 metres above the flat plain.
In English it used to be called Ayers Rock, after the politician Henry Ayers.
For the Anangu, Uluru is sacred.
Since October 2019, climbing it has been banned.

abschnitte.text: **Uluru** stands in the **Northern Territory**, almost in the middle of **Australia**. It is a mighty rock of **sandstone** and several kilometres long. It rises about **348 metres** above the plain, which is higher than the Eiffel Tower. Around Uluru the land is **dry and flat**. It is a hot area with little rain.

Uluru glows **reddish**. The colour comes from iron in the rock, which rusts in the air. At **sunrise** and **sunset** the rock looks especially strongly red, sometimes almost glowing. Many visitors come at exactly these times to see the play of colour. After a rare rainfall, waterfalls flow over the rock.

In **1873** an explorer named the rock after the politician **Henry Ayers**. That is why it was called **Ayers Rock** in English. Today the Aboriginal name, **Uluru**, is used again. Since 1985 the land has officially belonged to the **Anangu** again. They manage the national park together with the Australian government.

The **Anangu** are the Aboriginal people who live around Uluru. For them the rock is **sacred**. Many places tell stories from the **Dreamtime**, and some of them may not be photographed. Since **26 October 2019**, **climbing** Uluru has been banned. In this way the holy place of the Anangu is respected. Visitors can, however, walk on a path round the rock.

gewusst: The Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The path round Uluru is about ten kilometres long.

teile.einleitung: The Four Noble Truths are the core of the Buddha’s teaching. They explain what suffering is, where it comes from, that it can end and what path leads to its end. The Buddha proclaimed them for the first time in Sarnath near Varanasi.
wichtigste: The first truth speaks of suffering, in Pali dukkha.
The second names greed and craving as the cause of suffering.
The third says that suffering can cease.
The fourth shows the way: the Eightfold Path.
The state without suffering is called nirvana.
The Buddha first proclaimed the truths in Sarnath.
They are often compared with the approach of a doctor.

abschnitte.text: The first truth says that life brings **suffering**. The word for it is **dukkha**. It means pain, but also dissatisfaction and the experience that nothing lasts for ever. Examples are illness, old age and the loss of something loved. The Buddha did not want to make people sad by this, but to look honestly.

The second truth names the **cause** of suffering. The Buddha spoke of **thirst**, in Pali **tanha**. What is meant is **greed**, craving and clinging to things. Anyone who always wants more or cannot let go will never be completely content. According to Buddhist teaching, this craving also holds people fast in **samsara**, the cycle of rebirths.

The third truth gives hope: suffering **can cease**. It ends when craving goes out entirely. This state is called **nirvana**, which literally means “going out”. What is meant is the end of greed, hatred and delusion. According to the teaching, anyone who reaches nirvana is also freed from the cycle of rebirths.

The fourth truth shows the **way** out of suffering: the **Eightfold Path**. This includes, for example, right understanding, right speech, right action and right mindfulness. The four truths are gladly compared with a **doctor**: he recognises the illness, finds the cause, says that a cure is possible and prescribes a treatment.

After his enlightenment the Buddha went to the **Deer Park** at **Sarnath** near Varanasi. There he explained the Four Noble Truths for the first time to five ascetics. This sermon is also called “the setting in motion of the wheel of the teaching”. That is why the **wheel** is still a sign of Buddhism today.

gewusst: All the great branches of Buddhism recognise the Four Noble Truths as a foundation.
According to tradition, the five listeners of the first sermon became the Buddha’s first monks.

teile.einleitung: Zhu Xi was a Chinese philosopher who lived from 1130 to 1200. He is regarded as the most important thinker of Neo-Confucianism. His teaching shaped education in China for centuries.
wichtigste: Zhu Xi lived in the time of the Southern Song dynasty.
He is regarded as the most important thinker of Neo-Confucianism.
At the centre is the pair of concepts li (principle) and qi (vital stuff).
He put together the Four Books with commentaries.
He stressed the investigation of things, in Chinese gewu.

abschnitte.text: **Zhu Xi** lived from **1130 to 1200** in the time of the **Southern Song dynasty**. He was an official, a teacher and a scholar. He combined the teachings of **Confucius** with new ideas about the world and about people. This school of thought is called **Neo-Confucianism**. Zhu Xi is regarded as its most important thinker.

For Zhu Xi, everything consists of two things. **Li** is the shaping **principle**, a kind of blueprint in every thing. **Qi** is the **vital stuff**, the material force of which things are made. The two always belong together. This li is a different character from the li that means rites and good manners.

Zhu Xi stressed the **investigation of things**, in Chinese **gewu**. By this he meant examining the principle in individual things closely. In this way a person is to gain **knowledge** and **moral clarity** step by step. For him, learning was therefore a path to becoming a good person.

Zhu Xi put together the **Four Books** and wrote **commentaries** on them. They are the **Analects** of Confucius, the **Mencius**, the **Great Learning** and the **Doctrine of the Mean**. With his explanations they became the basic text of education. Later, candidates in the state **civil service examinations** in China had to know these texts according to his interpretation.

gewusst: From the 14th century until 1905, the Four Books with Zhu Xi’s commentaries remained the basis of the Chinese civil service examinations.
Zhu Xi’s teaching also became very influential in Korea and Japan.

teile.einleitung: In many Buddhist temples in Asia, bells hang. Their deep, long sound calls the monks to prayer and is meant to calm people. Alongside them there are smaller sound instruments such as singing bowls and cymbals.
wichtigste: Large Japanese temple bells have no clapper inside.
They are struck from outside with a thick wooden beam.
In Japan the temple bell is struck 108 times on New Year’s Eve.
Bells call the monks to prayer and meditation.
Small wind bells hang at the roof corners of many pagodas.
Tibetan monks hold a hand bell together with a thunderbolt.

abschnitte.text: Japanese temple bells are often very large and cast from **bronze**. Unlike church bells in Europe they have **no clapper** inside. They are struck from outside with a thick, horizontally hung **wooden beam**. This produces a deep note that rings on for a long time. Similar bells are found in China and Korea too.

In Japan the temple bell is struck **108 times** on **New Year’s Eve**. According to Buddhist teaching there are **108 desires** and bad wishes that make a person restless. Each stroke is meant to drive one of them away. Many people come to the temple at night, listen and are sometimes allowed to strike it once themselves. In this way the new year begins with a pure heart.

In the monastery the sound of the bell tells the monks when it is time for **prayer** and **meditation**. In this way the day begins and ends. The deep, long note is meant to bring **calm** to the heart. People listen to it attentively until it has died away completely. The **singing bowl**, a bowl made of metal, is used in the same way: when you strike it, it rings for a long time and quietly.

At the corners of the roofs of many **pagodas** hang **small wind bells**. The wind makes them ring. Tibetan monks hold a small **hand bell** in the left hand and a **thunderbolt**, in Tibetan a **dorje**, in the right. The two belong together. The **tingsha** are two small metal discs on a cord. You strike them lightly together and hear a bright note.

gewusst: Some temple bells in Japan weigh several dozen tonnes.
The number 108 is special in Buddhism: many Buddhist prayer chains also have 108 beads.

teile.einleitung: The Tanakh is the holy scripture of Judaism. It contains stories, laws, prayers and the words of the prophets. Christians took over these writings and call them the Old Testament.
wichtigste: Tanakh is an invented word from T, N and K: Torah, Nevi’im (Prophets) and Ketuvim (Writings).
According to the Jewish count, the Tanakh has 24 books.
Christians often count the same texts as 39 books.
The Tanakh is written almost entirely in Hebrew, with some parts of Daniel and Ezra in Aramaic.
In the Jewish order it ends with Chronicles.
From 1947, scrolls over 2,000 years old were found at Qumran by the Dead Sea.

abschnitte.text: The word **Tanakh** is formed from the initial letters of the three parts. **T** stands for the **Torah**, the five books of Moses. **N** stands for the **Nevi’im**, the Prophets. **K** stands for the **Ketuvim**, the Writings. Because the K at the end of a word sounds like “kh” in Hebrew, people say Tanakh.

The **Prophets** include books about the history of Israel, such as Joshua and Kings, and the books of the prophets themselves. **Isaiah** is regarded as one of the great prophets. The **Writings** include the **Psalms**, Proverbs, the Book of Ruth and many more. In the Jewish order, the books of **Chronicles** come at the very end.

According to the Jewish count, the Tanakh has **24 books**. Christians often divide the same texts into **39 books**. For example, they count the twelve minor prophets individually, whereas in Judaism they form a single book. In the Christian **Old Testament** the order is also partly different. It usually ends with the prophet **Malachi**.

Almost the whole Tanakh is written in **Hebrew**. A few chapters in the books of **Daniel** and **Ezra**, however, are in **Aramaic**, the common language of the Orient at the time. Already in antiquity the Tanakh was translated into Greek. This translation is called the **Septuagint**, which means “seventy”, because according to legend 72 scholars worked on it.

From **1947** many ancient scrolls were discovered in caves near **Qumran** by the **Dead Sea**. A shepherd found the first ones. The scrolls are over 2,000 years old and contain texts from almost all the books of the Tanakh. For research this was a sensation: you could see how carefully the texts were copied over many centuries.

gewusst: Among the Qumran finds is an almost complete scroll of the Book of Isaiah.
The Book of Esther is the only book of the Tanakh that has so far not been found among the Qumran scrolls.

teile.einleitung: The Torah is the most important part of the holy scripture of Judaism. It consists of the five books of Moses. In the synagogue it is read aloud from a precious, hand-written Torah scroll.
wichtigste: The Torah consists of the five books of Moses.
The first book is called Genesis, the fifth Deuteronomy.
A Torah scroll is written by hand on parchment.
The scroll is attached to two wooden rollers.
When reading, you point at the lines with a pointer, the yad.
In the synagogue the Torah scroll is kept in the Torah ark.
At 13, a boy reads aloud from the Torah for the first time at his bar mitzvah.

abschnitte.text: The **Torah** consists of the **five books of Moses**. The first book is called **Genesis**, in Hebrew **Bereshit**, which means “In the beginning”. It tells from the creation of the world to Joseph in Egypt. After that follow Exodus, Leviticus and Numbers. The fifth and last book is called **Deuteronomy**, in Hebrew **Devarim**. It ends with the death of Moses.

abschnitte.titel: How a Torah scroll is made
abschnitte.text: A Torah scroll is written **by hand**. This is done by a specially trained **scribe**, in Hebrew a **sofer**. He writes with a quill and ink on **parchment**, which is made from animal skin and lasts a very long time. Every letter must be exactly right, because a scroll with mistakes may not be used. For a whole scroll the scribe often needs many months.

The scroll is attached to **two wooden rollers**. When reading, you roll it from one roller onto the other. The holy scripture is not supposed to be touched with the fingers. That is why you point at the lines with a **pointer**. It is called a **yad**, which means “hand”, and often looks like a small hand with an outstretched finger.

In the **synagogue** the Torah scroll is kept in the **Torah ark**, a beautiful cupboard on the wall that faces Jerusalem. Often the scroll is adorned with an embroidered mantle and silver decoration. In the service a particular section is read aloud every week. In this way the whole Torah is read through once in the course of a year.

At **13**, a Jewish boy celebrates his **bar mitzvah**. From then on he is regarded in the religion as an adult and may read aloud from the Torah for the first time. Girls celebrate a **bat mitzvah** at 12. At the festival of **Simchat Torah**, “joy of the Torah”, the year’s reading ends and begins again right away from the start. Then people dance with the Torah scrolls through the synagogue.

gewusst: A Torah scroll contains over 300,000 Hebrew letters.
A complete Torah scroll can weigh many kilograms and be several dozen metres long.

teile.einleitung: The Tibet Institute Rikon in the canton of Zurich is a Buddhist monastery in the middle of Switzerland. It is regarded as the first Tibetan monastery outside Asia. It arose because Switzerland took in Tibetan refugees in the 1960s.
wichtigste: The Tibet Institute stands in Rikon in the Töss valley, in the municipality of Zell in the canton of Zurich.
It was consecrated on 9 November 1968.
It is regarded as the first Tibetan Buddhist monastery outside Asia.
The brothers Henri and Jacques Kuhn suggested the founding and provided the land.
From 1961 Switzerland took in Tibetan refugees in larger numbers.
Officially it was called an “institute”, because the Federal Constitution at that time banned new monasteries.
In 2018 the Dalai Lama attended the 50th anniversary.

abschnitte.text: After the failed **Tibetan uprising of 1959**, many Tibetans fled their homeland, mostly to **India** and **Nepal**. The **Dalai Lama** too had to flee. From **1961**, **Switzerland** was one of the first Western countries to take in Tibetan refugees in larger numbers. Today one of the largest Tibetan communities in Europe lives in Switzerland.

In **Rikon** in the **Töss valley**, the brothers **Henri and Jacques Kuhn** ran a **metalware factory**. Many Tibetan refugees found work there. The brothers noticed that the people missed their religion and culture. So they suggested the founding of a monastery and provided the **land**. The foundation stone was laid in 1967, and on **9 November 1968** the institute was consecrated.

The **Federal Constitution** of 1874 banned the founding of **new monasteries** in Switzerland. That is why the monastery was officially called an **“institute”**. This ban was lifted only in **1973** in a popular vote. In the Tibet Institute a few **monks** live with their **abbot**. They look after the Tibetans in Switzerland and celebrate the Buddhist festivals.

The institute is also a place of scholarship. Its **library** comprises around 10,000 titles and is regarded as one of the most extensive collections on Tibet in the world. Researchers from many countries come here. Visitors can look round the monastery on certain days and learn more about Tibetan Buddhism.

In September **2018** the institute celebrated its **50th anniversary**. For this occasion the **14th Dalai Lama** came to Rikon. He had already visited the monastery several times. For the Tibetan community in Switzerland it was a great celebration.

gewusst: The Tibetan community in Switzerland today numbers several thousand people.

teile.einleitung: The Lord’s Prayer is the best-known prayer of Christians. According to the Bible, Jesus himself taught it to his disciples. Christians of all churches pray it to this day.
wichtigste: The Lord’s Prayer is the most important shared prayer of all Christians.
According to the Bible, Jesus taught his disciples this prayer.
It begins with the words “Our Father in heaven”.
The prayer is found in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke.
It is prayed in services, at baptisms and at home.

abschnitte.text: The Lord’s Prayer is in the **New Testament** of the Bible. The longer version is found in the **Gospel of Matthew** in the Sermon on the Mount, a shorter one in the **Gospel of Luke**. There the disciples ask Jesus: “Lord, teach us to pray.” Jesus answers with this prayer. In Latin it is called the **Pater noster**.

First God is addressed and praised as **Father**. Then follow several **requests**: that God’s kingdom come and his will be done. People ask for their daily **bread**, that is, for what they need to live. They also ask for **forgiveness** and promise to forgive others themselves. At the end comes the request to be kept from evil.

Catholics, Reformed Christians, Orthodox Christians and many other Christians pray the Lord’s Prayer. That is why it is regarded as a prayer that **unites** the churches. It is spoken in the **service**, at baptisms, weddings and funerals. Many people learn it as children. It has been translated into hundreds of languages.

gewusst: In Switzerland, Reformed and Catholic Christians have prayed a shared German version of the Lord’s Prayer since the 1970s.
At the end of many versions there is a doxology: “For yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory.”

teile.einleitung: Thor is a god from Norse mythology. He is the god of thunder and one of the strongest gods. His famous weapon is a hammer.
wichtigste: Thor is the thunder god of the Germanic peoples and the Vikings.
His weapon is a hammer that returns to him after every throw.
His chariot is pulled by two goats.
Among the southern Germanic peoples he was called Donar.
His father is Odin, the chief god.
His greatest enemy is the Midgard Serpent.

abschnitte.text: Among the **Germanic peoples** and the **Vikings**, Thor was the god of **thunder and storms**. When it thundered, people believed that Thor was driving across the sky. He was regarded as protector of the gods and of humans. Many farmers revered him, because thunderstorms also bring rain for the fields. Among the southern Germanic peoples he was called **Donar**, a word that recalls “thunder”.

Thor’s weapon is a mighty **hammer** named **Mjölnir**. According to the sagas, after every throw the hammer returns to Thor’s hand as if by itself. Many people wore small **hammer pendants** as lucky charms and for protection. Pendants like this from the Viking age have been found in many places in northern Europe.

Thor drives in a **chariot** pulled by **two goats**. People imagined that the rolling of his chariot sounds like thunder. In one saga Thor slaughters the goats in the evening to feed his guests. The next morning he brings them back to life with his hammer.

Thor’s father is **Odin**, the chief god of the Norse sagas. Odin has only one eye and is accompanied by two ravens that bring him news from the world. Thor is one of the strongest gods of all. His wife is called **Sif** and has golden hair. The gods live in a world called **Asgard**.

abschnitte.titel: The fight against the Midgard Serpent
abschnitte.text: Thor’s greatest enemy is the **Midgard Serpent**. It is so long that in the sea it reaches round the whole world of humans. In one saga Thor almost fishes it out of the sea. At the end of the world, called **Ragnarök**, the two fight one last time. Thor defeats the serpent but dies of its poison.

gewusst: The weekday Thursday is named after Donar, that is, after Thor; in German it is Donnerstag.
The stories about Thor are found above all in the Edda, a collection from Iceland from the 13th century.

teile.einleitung: Wicca is a new religion that arose in England in the 20th century. Its followers revere nature and celebrate festivals through the year. Wicca is one of the neo-pagan religions.
wichtigste: The Englishman Gerald Gardner is regarded as its founder.
Gardner made Wicca publicly known in the 1950s.
His book “Witchcraft Today” appeared in 1954.
The most important guiding principle is the “Wiccan Rede”: if it harms nobody, do what you will.
Wicca celebrates eight festivals of the wheel of the year, the sabbats.
Doreen Valiente reworked many ritual texts.

abschnitte.text: **Gerald Gardner** is regarded as the founder of the modern Wicca religion. He made it publicly known in England in the **1950s**. In **1954** his book **“Witchcraft Today”** appeared. In it he presented Wicca as an old witch religion that had survived in secret. Historians today, however, see Wicca as a **new religion** of the 20th century that takes up older ideas.

**Doreen Valiente** belonged to Gardner’s group. She rewrote several ritual texts in poetic form, including the **“Charge of the Goddess”**. That is why she is often called the “mother of modern witchcraft”. Later others founded branches of their own, such as **Alex Sanders**. **Raymond Buckland** spread Wicca in the USA.

The most important ethical guiding principle is called the **“Wiccan Rede”**. In English it reads “An it harm none, do what ye will”. That means: **if it harms nobody, do what you will.** So every person is to act freely but take responsibility for the consequences. Many Wicca groups revere a **goddess** and a **god** and regard nature as sacred.

Wicca celebrates **eight** festivals of the year, the **sabbats**. They include the two **solstices** and the two **equinoxes**. In between lie four further festivals, such as **Samhain** in autumn and **Beltane** in spring. Together they form the **Wheel of the Year**. Many festivals go back to old customs of the Celts and Germanic peoples.

gewusst: The word “Wicca” comes from Old English, where it meant roughly “sorcerer”.
Samhain is regarded as one of the forerunners of today’s Halloween.

teile.einleitung: Swami Vivekananda was an Indian monk and teacher who lived from 1863 to 1902. He made Hinduism and yoga known in the West. In India he is still greatly revered.
wichtigste: Vivekananda’s birth name was Narendranath Datta, and he was born in Calcutta in 1863.
His teacher was the mystic Ramakrishna.
In 1893 he became famous at the Parliament of the World’s Religions in Chicago.
His book “Raja Yoga” appeared in 1896.
In 1897 he founded the Ramakrishna Mission.
He represented Advaita Vedanta in particular.
His birthday, 12 January, is National Youth Day in India.

abschnitte.text: Vivekananda was originally called **Narendranath Datta**. He was born in **1863** in **Calcutta** and studied Western philosophy. In Calcutta he met the mystic **Ramakrishna**. He became his most important pupil. After Ramakrishna’s death he became a monk and took the name **Vivekananda**.

In **1893** Vivekananda travelled to the USA for the **Parliament of the World’s Religions** in **Chicago**. He began his speech with the words “Sisters and Brothers of America”. For this he received great applause. He spoke about **tolerance** and about how all religions can lead to the same goal. Afterwards he gave many lectures in the USA and in Europe.

Vivekananda put **Advaita Vedanta** especially in the foreground. This teaching says that the divine is in everything and in every person. From this he concluded that you serve God when you **help people**. In 1896 his book **“Raja Yoga”** appeared, based on lectures in New York. It explained the **Yoga Sutras** of Patanjali and made yoga known in the West.

In **1897** Vivekananda founded the **Ramakrishna Mission**. It combines spirituality with practical help. The mission runs schools and hospitals and helps in disasters. Its seat is in **Belur** near Calcutta. Vivekananda died already in **1902**, at only 39 years old.

The French writer **Romain Rolland** lived for a long time in **Villeneuve** on Lake Geneva. He received the Nobel Prize in Literature. Around 1930 he wrote biographies of Ramakrishna and Vivekananda. In this way he made the two Indian thinkers known in Europe. His books are still translated into many languages today.

gewusst: Since 1985 India has celebrated Vivekananda’s birthday on 12 January as National Youth Day.
At the southern tip of India, the Vivekananda Rock Memorial stands on a rock in the sea.

teile.einleitung: In Norse mythology, Valhalla is the magnificent hall of the god Odin. According to the belief of the Vikings, the warriors who fell in battle went there. There they waited for the last great battle at the end of the world.
wichtigste: Valhalla was the hall of the warriors who fell in battle.
The lord of Valhalla was Odin, the chief god.
The Valkyries brought the fallen to Valhalla.
The warriors in Valhalla are called the Einherjar.
According to the Edda, the roof was covered with shields.
The boar Sæhrímnir and the goat Heidrun provided for the warriors.
The warriors prepared for Ragnarök.

abschnitte.text: **Valhalla** means roughly “hall of the fallen”. It belonged to **Odin**, the chief god of Norse mythology. There he gathered the best warriors around him. We know Valhalla mainly from the **Edda**, a collection of old songs and tales from Iceland. According to the Edda, the roof was covered with **shields** and the rafters were spear shafts.

The **Valkyries** were female figures in Odin’s service. They rode over the battlefields and chose who should fall. The word means roughly “choosers of the slain”. They brought the fallen to Valhalla. There they also handed the warriors their drinking horns.

The warriors in Valhalla are called **Einherjar**. Every day they practised fighting, and in the evening they feasted together. For food there was the boar **Sæhrímnir**. It was cooked every evening and was whole again the next morning. The goat **Heidrun** stands on the roof and feeds on the tree **Lærad**. From her udder flows **mead**, a honey wine.

At the end of the world, according to the saga, **Ragnarök** comes. Then gods and giants fight against each other. The Einherjar are to stand at **Odin’s side**. That is why they practised in Valhalla every day. According to the Edda, Ragnarök ends with the fall of the old world, from which a new one arises.

gewusst: In Bavaria there is a building called the Walhalla, a hall of fame for famous Germans, built in the 19th century.
According to the Edda, Valhalla has over 500 doors, through each of which 800 warriors can march at the same time.

teile.einleitung: Tolerance means letting other people be, with their opinions, their faith and their customs. In a school with children from many cultures especially, this is important. Tolerance helps people to live together peacefully.
wichtigste: The word tolerance comes from the Latin “tolerare”, which means “to bear” or “to put up with”.
Respect means honouring the dietary rules and festivals of others.
Anyone who asks questions out of interest learns something new and breaks down prejudices.
Conversations between people of different religions are called interreligious dialogue.
In Switzerland there is a Week of Religions every year in November.
Nobody may be laughed at or excluded because of their faith.

abschnitte.text: The word **tolerance** comes from the Latin **“tolerare”**, which means “to bear” or “to put up with”. A tolerant person lets other people be, with their **faith**, their opinion and their customs, even if they themselves think differently. That does not mean you have to like everything. But you respect the others and treat them fairly. In Switzerland the **Federal Constitution** protects **freedom of belief and conscience**: every person may freely choose their religion or have none.

A classmate does not eat pork because of her religion? Then it is respectful simply to **accept** that. Everyone may live by their own dietary rules. If a friend celebrates a festival you do not know, you can **ask with interest**. Anyone who listens learns something new. When you visit a **house of worship** that is not your own, you are quiet and keep to the rules, because for many it is a holy place.

A **prejudice** is an opinion about other people without really knowing them. For example, you think all people of a certain religion are the same. Such judgements are often wrong and can hurt. Anyone who gets to know others and talks with them can **break down** prejudices. Often you then notice that you have many things in common.

In **interreligious dialogue**, people of different religions talk with one another. They learn from each other, look for **things in common** and respect **differences**. In Switzerland every year in the first week of November there is the **Week of Religions**. Across the country over 100 events take place at which you can get to know mosques, temples, churches and synagogues.

Sometimes a child is **laughed at** or excluded because of their religion. That is not right. The right thing is to **stand by** the child and to **get help**, for example from a teacher. That takes courage. Anyone who acts in this way shows respect and helps everyone in the class to feel at ease.

gewusst: UNESCO has declared 16 November the International Day for Tolerance.
In Lessing’s play “Nathan the Wise”, the famous ring parable tells of three religions that could all be equally valuable.

teile.einleitung: Tibetan Buddhism is a form of Buddhism that developed in Tibet and the Himalayas. It is known for colourful prayer flags, mantras and the Dalai Lama. Today it has followers all over the world, including in Switzerland.
wichtigste: According to tradition, Padmasambhava brought Buddhism to Tibet in the 8th century.
Tibetan Buddhism is also called Vajrayana, “diamond vehicle”.
There are four great schools; the Dalai Lama belongs to the Gelug school.
The best-known mantra is “Om mani padme hum”.
The 14th Dalai Lama received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989 and lives in Dharamsala in India.
A tulku is a teacher who is regarded as the rebirth of a former master.

abschnitte.text: According to tradition, the master **Padmasambhava** brought Buddhism from India to Tibet in the **8th century**. In Tibet he is revered as **“Guru Rinpoche”**, which means “precious master”. Tibetan Buddhism is also called **Vajrayana**, “diamond vehicle”. Vajra means diamond or thunderbolt. It uses special methods such as **mantras**, rituals and visualisations, that is, inner images.

There are **four great schools**: Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya and **Gelug**. The **Dalai Lama** belongs to the Gelug school, which was founded by **Tsongkhapa**. It is also called the school of the **“Yellow Hats”**. A special teacher can be recognised as a **tulku**, as the conscious rebirth of a deceased master. The Dalai Lama too is found in this way.

After the **Tibetan uprising of 1959**, the 14th Dalai Lama fled to **India**. Since 1960, **Dharamsala**, more precisely the district of McLeod Ganj, has been the seat of the Tibetan government in exile. In **1989** the Dalai Lama received the **Nobel Peace Prize** for his non-violent work for Tibet. In **Lhasa** stands the **Potala Palace**, formerly the winter palace of the Dalai Lamas. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994 and is now a museum.

The best-known mantra is **“Om mani padme hum”**. It is dedicated to the **bodhisattva of compassion**, an enlightened being who wants to help others. The mantra is spoken, sung and carved on stones. Everywhere in Tibet colourful **prayer flags** flutter in the wind. They are printed with mantras, and according to the belief the wind carries the blessings out into the world.

From **1961** Switzerland took in Tibetan refugees. In **Rikon** in the canton of Zurich, the **Tibet Institute** arose in 1968, which is regarded as the first Tibetan monastery outside Asia. Today there is a large Tibetan community in Switzerland and several Buddhist centres.

gewusst: Prayer flags come in five colours: blue, white, red, green and yellow.
The Potala Palace stands at around 3,700 metres above sea level and has over a thousand rooms.

teile.einleitung: The Surb valley is a valley in the canton of Aargau, named after the river Surb. It is a special place in Swiss history: in the villages of Endingen and Lengnau, Jews were for a long time allowed to live in the only places in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Surb valley lies in the canton of Aargau.
In Endingen and Lengnau, the only Jewish communities in Switzerland lived for a long time.
Until 1866, Jews in Switzerland were allowed to live only in these two villages.
Old synagogues still stand in both villages.
Between the villages lies an old Jewish cemetery.

abschnitte.text: In the 18th century, Jews in the Confederation were allowed to live only in **Endingen** and **Lengnau**. They were allowed to live there but had far fewer rights than their Christian neighbours. They were forbidden to buy land or to practise many crafts. Many therefore worked as traders, for example in cattle or cloth. Even so, Jews and Christians lived closely side by side in the villages.

In both villages there are still **synagogues** from the 19th century. They are among the oldest in Switzerland. Between Endingen and Lengnau lies an old **Jewish cemetery**, where people from both communities were buried. A **cultural trail** now leads to these places and tells their story.

Only in **1866** did Jews in Switzerland receive the right to settle anywhere. With the Federal Constitution of **1874** they also received full freedom of belief. After that many families moved from the Surb valley to cities such as Zurich, Basel or Baden. Today only a few Jews live in the Surb valley, but the buildings recall this long history.

gewusst: The Jewish communities of Endingen and Lengnau had to bury their dead for a long time on an island in the Rhine before they received a cemetery of their own.

teile.einleitung: Varanasi is one of the oldest cities in India and for Hindus the holiest place on the river Ganges. Every year millions of pilgrims come to pray, to bathe in the river and to honour the dead.
wichtigste: Varanasi lies in the north of India in the state of Uttar Pradesh.
The city is regarded as the holy city of the god Shiva.
An old name is Kashi, “the luminous”; in English it used to be called Benares.
On the bank, broad stone steps, the ghats, lead down to the Ganges.
At the Manikarnika Ghat the dead are cremated.
Every evening the fire ceremony Ganga Aarti takes place at the river.
Near Varanasi lies Sarnath, an important place of Buddhism.

abschnitte.text: Varanasi is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. For Hindus it is the city of the god **Shiva**. One of his most important temples is the **Kashi Vishwanath Temple** in the middle of the old town. The old name **Kashi** means roughly “the luminous”. Under the British the city was called **Benares**.

On the west bank of the Ganges many **ghats** line up one after another. These are broad stone steps leading right into the water. Here believers bathe early in the morning in the holy river, pray and bring offerings of flowers. The Ganges is called **Ganga** in Hindi and is revered as a goddess. Anyone who bathes in it hopes to be cleansed of bad deeds.

At some ghats, especially the **Manikarnika Ghat**, the dead are **cremated** on wood fires. The fires burn there almost without a break. Many Hindus believe in a **cycle of rebirth**. According to their belief, anyone who dies in Varanasi is **released** from this cycle. That is why some old people come to the city to spend their last days here.

Every evening the **Ganga Aarti** takes place on the bank. Priests swing large oil lamps in time with chants and bells. In this way they honour the river as a goddess. Thousands of people watch from the steps and from boats. Many set small lights on leaves into the water.

About 10 kilometres from Varanasi lies **Sarnath**. Here, according to tradition, the **Buddha** gave his first sermon. That is why Sarnath is an important place of pilgrimage for Buddhists. The area also has a meaning for the **Jains**. Varanasi is thus a place where several religions meet.

gewusst: Varanasi is one of the oldest cities in the world that has been continuously inhabited for thousands of years.
On the bank at Varanasi there are over 80 ghats.

teile.einleitung: Vesak, also called Vesakh, is the most important festival in Buddhism. On a single day Buddhists remember the Buddha’s birth, his enlightenment and his death. It is celebrated with lights, prayers and good deeds.
wichtigste: At the Vesak festival people celebrate the Buddha’s birth, enlightenment and death.
The festival is on the full-moon day of the month of Vesakha, usually in May.
Because it follows the moon, the date is different every year.
In Sri Lanka, colourful lanterns decorate the streets.
Many people share food with the needy.
The UN recognised Vesak as an international day in 1999.

abschnitte.text: Vesak is celebrated on the **full-moon day**. The name comes from the lunar month **Vesakha**, which usually falls in **May**. Because the lunar calendar differs from our calendar, the date changes every year. Many Buddhist festivals follow the moon. In some countries Vesak is a public holiday.

According to tradition in many countries, three important events happened at a full moon in the same month. The Buddha was **born**, he attained **enlightenment** and he died. All three are celebrated together at Vesak. Believers visit temples, pray and listen to sermons. Some countries celebrate the Buddha’s birth on a day of its own.

In **Sri Lanka** people hang up countless colourful **lanterns**. At night whole streets glow. In **South Korea**, **lotus lanterns** decorate the temples for the Buddha’s birthday, and there are great processions with them. In Buddhism light stands for wisdom and insight.

A lovely custom is **pouring water** over a small figure of the baby Buddha. This recalls his birth. At Vesak many Buddhists try to do especially **good deeds**. They share **food** and drinks with the needy and with strangers. Some also set captive animals free.

gewusst: The United Nations recognised Vesak as an international day in 1999.
In Sri Lanka at Vesak there is free food and drink for everyone at roadside stalls.

teile.einleitung: In Islam, wudu is the ritual washing before prayer. Before Muslims pray, they wash their hands, face, arms and feet. In this way they prepare themselves physically and inwardly for prayer.
wichtigste: Wudu is the minor ritual washing in Islam.
Muslims do it before prayer.
The hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head and feet are washed.
The washing follows a fixed order.
Mosques have washrooms or fountains of their own for it.

abschnitte.text: Muslims pray **five times** a day. Before prayer they perform the washing called **wudu**. The word comes from Arabic. The washing is meant to cleanse the body and shows respect for God. At the same time it helps you to become calm and to **concentrate** on the prayer.

First you say inwardly that you want to wash for prayer. Then you wash the **hands** and rinse the **mouth** and **nose**. After that come the **face** and the **arms** up to the elbows. With wet hands you wipe over the **head** and the ears. Finally you wash the **feet** up to the ankles.

In **mosques** there are washrooms or fountains with many taps of their own. Many people can wash there at the same time. In mosques in **Switzerland** too there are such washing places. If no water is available, according to Islamic teaching you may use clean sand or earth instead. This substitute washing is called **tayammum**.

gewusst: Many mosques have a beautiful fountain in the courtyard for the washing.
According to the teaching, you do not have to repeat the washing before every prayer as long as it is still valid.

teile.einleitung: According to the Bible, the people of Israel consisted of twelve tribes. Each tribe goes back to a son of the patriarch Jacob, who was also called Israel. The tribes play an important role in many stories of the Bible.
wichtigste: According to the Bible, the twelve tribes go back to the twelve sons of Jacob.
The tribe of Levi served at the sanctuary and received no land of its own.
Joseph’s sons Ephraim and Manasseh became the forefathers of tribes of their own.
The word “Jews” comes from the tribe of Judah.
King David came from Judah, King Saul from Benjamin.
The tribes of the northern kingdom are called the ten lost tribes.

abschnitte.text: The first book of the Bible tells of **Jacob**, who later received the name **Israel**. Jacob had **twelve sons**, among them Reuben, Levi, Judah, Joseph and Benjamin. Each of them is regarded as the **forefather** of a tribe. The descendants were therefore called the **Israelites**, that is, the children of Israel.

abschnitte.titel: Levi and the sons of Joseph
abschnitte.text: The tribe of **Levi** was responsible for worship. The **Levites** therefore received no tribal territory of their own, only individual towns. The priests also came from among them. In return there is no tribe of Joseph: Jacob adopted Joseph’s sons **Ephraim** and **Manasseh** as his own sons. In this way two tribes arose, and when the land was divided it still came to twelve territories.

The first king of Israel was **Saul**, the son of Kish from the tribe of **Benjamin**. The prophet **Samuel** anointed him king. After him ruled **David**, who came from **Bethlehem** in the territory of the tribe of **Judah**. David’s family afterwards ruled the kingdom of Judah for a long time.

Later the kingdom split into two parts. In the north lay the kingdom of **Israel**, in the south the kingdom of **Judah**. The inhabitants of the south were called **Judeans**, and from this came the word **Jews**. Around 722 BC the **Assyrians** conquered the northern kingdom and deported many people. These tribes have been called the **ten lost tribes** ever since.

gewusst: To this day there are legends and speculations about where the ten lost tribes may have ended up.
Because Levi received no land and Joseph is represented by two sons, there are still twelve tribal territories.

teile.einleitung: A ziggurat is a gigantic stepped tower from ancient Mesopotamia, the land between the Euphrates and the Tigris. On its summit stood a temple for a deity. Ziggurats are among the oldest great structures of humankind.
wichtigste: Ziggurats are stepped towers from Mesopotamia and Elam.
They consisted mainly of mud bricks.
On the top level stood a high temple for the deity.
In the 21st century BC, King Ur-Nammu had the great ziggurat of Ur built.
The ziggurat Chogha Zanbil in Iran is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The ziggurat was regarded as a link between heaven and earth.

abschnitte.text: In the land between the two rivers there was hardly any natural stone but plenty of mud. That is why people built their ziggurats of **mud bricks**. The core consisted of air-dried bricks. The outer shell was often of **fired bricks**, which are harder and more weatherproof. **Bitumen**, a natural, sticky pitch, was often used as mortar.

abschnitte.titel: A temple right at the top
abschnitte.text: A ziggurat had several levels that grew smaller towards the top. You reached the top by stairs or ramps. According to ancient accounts, on the top level stood a **high temple** for the city’s deity. The Greek historian **Herodotus** described such a temple on the ziggurat of Babylon. The structures were regarded as a link between **heaven and earth**.

One of the best-known ziggurats stands in **Ur**, in present-day **Iraq**. King **Ur-Nammu**, the founder of the Third Dynasty of Ur, began the building in the 21st century BC. His son **Shulgi** completed it. Today an impressive ruin of the complex remains, whose lower part was partly restored in the 20th century.

Ziggurats were not found only in Mesopotamia. In the kingdom of **Elam**, in the area of present-day **Iran**, King **Untash-Napirisha** had the ziggurat **Chogha Zanbil** built in the 13th century BC. It is regarded as one of the best-preserved ziggurats of all. Today it is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

gewusst: Many researchers suspect that the story of the Tower of Babel was inspired by the great ziggurat in Babylon.
Because stone was scarce, millions of mud bricks were needed for one ziggurat.

teile.einleitung: The names of our days of the week are very old. Many recall heavenly bodies or gods of the Romans and Germanic peoples. If you compare English, French and German, you discover exciting connections.
wichtigste: Sunday is named after the sun and Monday after the moon.
The English Tuesday is the day of the Germanic god Tyr.
The English Wednesday is the day of Woden.
Friday is named after the goddess Frija or Frigg.
French contains Roman gods: mardi for Mars, mercredi for Mercury, jeudi for Jupiter, vendredi for Venus.
The English Saturday is the day of Saturn.

abschnitte.text: Already the **Romans** named the days of the week after the seven heavenly bodies known at the time. **Sunday** is the day of the **sun**. **Monday** is the day of the **moon**. In French too, **“lundi”** recalls the moon, in Latin “luna”. In German the days are called “Sonntag” and “Montag”.

The other heavenly bodies bore the names of **Roman gods**. In French you can still see this clearly. **“Mardi”** is the day of the war god **Mars**, that is, Tuesday. **“Mercredi”** belongs to **Mercury**, that is, Wednesday. **“Jeudi”** is the day of **Jupiter**, Thursday, and **“vendredi”** the day of **Venus**, Friday.

The Germanic peoples took over the week from the Romans. But they often put in their **own gods**. The English **“Tuesday”** is the day of the god **Tiw**, called **Tyr** in the north, a god of battle and law. **“Wednesday”** comes from “Woden’s day”, the day of **Woden**. **Friday** is named after the goddess **Frija**, who was called **Frigg** in the north and was Odin’s wife.

Some German names have other origins. **Mittwoch** simply means “middle of the week”. The English **“Saturday”** is the day of the Roman god **Saturn**. In German we say **Samstag**, a word connected with the Jewish **Sabbath**. In northern Germany people also say Sonnabend.

gewusst: Thursday is named after the Germanic thunder god Donar, Thor in the north, which is why it is Donnerstag in German.
In Romansh, Wednesday is “mesemna”, so likewise the middle of the week.

teile.einleitung: Sukkot, the Feast of Tabernacles, is one of the great festivals in Judaism. For a week Jewish families eat in a hut they have built themselves. The festival recalls the wandering through the desert and is at the same time a harvest thanksgiving.
wichtigste: For Sukkot you build a small hut, the sukkah.
The roof is made of branches and foliage.
Through the roof you should be able to see the stars at night.
The festival recalls the wandering through the desert after the Exodus from Egypt.
Sukkot lasts seven days and falls in autumn.
The citrus fruit etrog is part of the festive bouquet.

abschnitte.text: For Sukkot you build a small **hut** in the garden, the yard or on the balcony. In Hebrew it is called a **sukkah**, and the plural is sukkot. That is why the festival is also called the **Feast of Tabernacles**. The roof is made of **branches**, **foliage** or reeds. It must not be solid and dense. Many children decorate the hut with fruit and pictures.

The roof is built so loosely that you can see the **stars** at night. Even so, there should be more shade than sun. During the festival people eat their meals in the hut. Some even sleep in it if the weather allows. In Switzerland, Jewish communities often build shared huts at the synagogue too.

The festival recalls the time after the **Exodus from Egypt**. According to the Bible, the people of Israel wandered for a long time through the **desert**. There they lived in simple huts. Sukkot is also one of the three **pilgrimage festivals**, together with Passover and Shavuot. In ancient times people made pilgrimages to the Temple in Jerusalem for these festivals.

Sukkot falls in **autumn**, in September or October, and lasts **seven days**. It is also a festival of thanks for the **harvest**. The festive bouquet includes a palm branch, myrtle and willow branches and the **etrog**. The etrog is a yellow citrus fruit that looks like a large lemon. Right after Sukkot come further festival days such as **Simchat Torah**, the joy of the Torah.

gewusst: The roof of a sukkah must be so loose that you can see the stars through the foliage.
The festive bouquet for Sukkot is made up of four different kinds of plant.

teile.einleitung: Vishnu is one of the most important gods of Hinduism. He is regarded as the preserver of the world and protects its order. Many Hindus revere him as the highest god.
wichtigste: In the Trimurti, Brahma is the creator, Vishnu the preserver and Shiva the destroyer.
Vishnu lives in the heavenly world of Vaikuntha.
His mount is Garuda, a giant bird.
In the primal ocean he rests on the many-headed serpent Shesha.
His consort is Lakshmi, the goddess of luck and prosperity.
He often holds a discus, a conch shell, a mace and a lotus flower.
His followers are called Vaishnavas.

abschnitte.text: In Hinduism, three gods form the **Trimurti**: **Brahma** creates, **Vishnu** preserves and **Shiva** destroys so that something new can arise. Vishnu keeps the **order** of the world. When evil gets the upper hand, he steps in. According to the belief, he then comes to earth in various forms. These forms are called **avatars**; well known are, for example, Rama and Krishna.

Vishnu lives in the heavenly world of **Vaikuntha**. For many of his devotees, reaching it is the highest goal. In many pictures Vishnu rests on the **primal ocean**. He lies on the huge, many-headed serpent **Shesha**. The serpent’s heads form a canopy over him.

Vishnu’s mount is **Garuda**, a mighty bird, half eagle and half human. He carries Vishnu through the air. Garuda is also an emblem animal, for example in Indonesia and Thailand. Vishnu’s consort is **Lakshmi**, the goddess of **luck** and **prosperity**. She is often shown sitting on a lotus flower.

Vishnu is usually shown with **four arms** and blue skin. In one hand he holds the **Sudarshana chakra**, a spinning discus. In another he carries the conch shell **shankha**, whose sound is meant to drive away evil. In addition there are a **mace** and a **lotus flower**. By these emblems he is recognised in pictures and statues.

Hindus who revere Vishnu as the highest god are called **Vaishnavas**. Their branch is called **Vaishnavism**. It is one of the largest branches of Hinduism. Many Vaishnavas revere Krishna or Rama especially as forms of Vishnu. In India there are countless temples to Vishnu.

gewusst: The Indonesian airline is called Garuda, after Vishnu’s mount.
According to the teaching, of Vishnu’s ten principal avatars nine have already appeared, and the tenth is yet to come.

teile.einleitung: Totem poles are tall, carved wooden trunks made by the peoples of the north-west coast of North America. They show animals and figures that tell the stories of families. Many stand in Canada and Alaska.
wichtigste: Totem poles are carved from large tree trunks, often from the wood of the western red cedar.
They come from the peoples of the north-west coast of North America.
The Haida in Canada and Alaska are famous carvers of totem poles.
Carved are animals such as bear, beaver, wolf, whale and, especially often, the raven.
Totem poles tell the history and origin of a family.
They are not images of gods and are not worshipped.
Many are painted in bright colours, for example red, black and blue-green.

abschnitte.text: A **totem pole** is carved from a large **tree trunk**. Usually the wood of the **western red cedar** is used. This wood is soft enough to carve and lasts a long time. The poles are set **upright** in the ground, often in front of houses or at the edge of villages. Some are more than ten metres tall.

abschnitte.titel: The peoples of the north-west coast
abschnitte.text: Totem poles come from the peoples of the **north-west coast of North America**, that is, from present-day **Canada** and **Alaska**. Especially well known are the **Haida**, who live on islands off the coast. The Tlingit and other peoples also carve totem poles. In the past they lived from fishing and were skilful woodworkers.

On totem poles, animals such as **bear**, **beaver**, **wolf**, **whale** or **eagle** are carved. Especially common is the **raven**. It is an important figure among the peoples of the north-west coast. In many stories it brings humans the **light**. Every figure has a meaning and stands for a family, an ancestor or a story.

Totem poles are **not images of gods** and are not worshipped. They show **crest animals** and tell the story and **origin** of a family or clan. Some commemorate a deceased person or an important event. Many are **painted in bright colours**, for example with red, black and blue-green. In this way the figures show up well.

gewusst: Totem poles also stand today in museums in Europe and in parks such as Stanley Park in Vancouver.
